st: Peel the taro (wear gloves if your skin gets itchy) and cut it into large chunks.
Put the chunks in a pot with the water and [[0.25 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Boil for 30 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). If using banana leaves, hold them over a flame for a few seconds to soften.
Stir the sugar and remaining salt into the coconut cream.
Place the taro on the leaves, pour the sweetened cream over, and wrap into tight parcels.
Bake for 30 minutes until the cream is bubbling and thick.
Open the parcels carefully, as steam will escape, and serve hot.
Peel the taro and grate it finely into a bowl, wearing gloves if needed.
Add [[0.5 cup]] coconut cream, the sugar and salt to the taro and mix into a thick paste.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Soften the banana leaves over a flame for a few seconds, and line a baking dish with them.
Spread the taro mixture in the dish and smooth the top.
Cover with leaves or foil and bake for 1 hour until set and slightly firm.
Pour [[1 cup]] coconut cream over the top and bake uncovered for 15 minutes more.
Let rest 10 minutes, then cut into squares.

ing: or spinach plus a few collard leaves
st: Wash the leaves, trim thick stems, and pat dry.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Mix the coconut cream, onion and salt.
Lay 3 or 4 leaves in a bundle on a banana leaf or foil sheet. Add some of the fish if using.
Spoon a few tablespoons of coconut mix into the center. Fold the leaves around to form a bundle.
Wrap in the banana leaf or foil and tie or seal tightly.
Bake for 45 minutes, until the leaves are very soft.
Unwrap carefully, stir gently, and serve hot.
Use only very fresh, sushi-grade tuna, kept cold. Cut it into small cubes about half an inch wide.
Put the tuna in a glass bowl with the lime juice and salt. Stir well.
Chill for [[20 minutes]], stirring once, until the fish turns opaque on the outside.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Add the onion, tomato and cucumber to the fish.
Pour the cold coconut milk over the top and stir gently.
Season with pepper and serve right away, very cold.

ing: whole cooked crab or crab legs
st: If the crab is live, ask your fishmonger to prepare it. Otherwise use fully cooked crab. Crack the shells so the sauce can reach the meat.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the coconut milk and add salt and pepper. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the crab, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, turning once.
Check that raw crab meat is firm and opaque. Cook 5 more minutes if not.
Serve in a bowl with sauce and lime wedges.
